sections.title: Executive Verdict
paragraphs: Prime Cable has demonstrated a real manufacturing scale-up, but revenue growth is not yet a reliable measure of underlying demand growth. Copper and aluminium reimbursement, a shift toward aerial-bunch cables, and a low pandemic base amplify nominal sales. The stronger claim is that sold cable length doubled between FY23 and FY25; the missing comparable physical-sales bridge and unresolved cost-record reliability prevent a clean underlying-growth score. An economic value-added cross-check is also supplied; the framework does not require tonnage mechanically.

The decisive obstacle is financing and cash realization. FY26 reported operating cash flow was negative ₹13.21 crore despite ₹12.24 crore profit. Receivables reached ₹70.52 crore, while most of the reported ₹12.87 crore cash was restricted or earmarked. A ₹39.9 crore expansion and rapid working-capital growth cannot be treated as self-financing merely because management expects strong sales.

Research Hold. Financial reliability and prospective funding gates remain on Hold, with no ordinary return or entry-price recommendation and no numerical ranking eligibility. This is not a finding of fraud, an observed default, or a prediction of insolvency. The explicit rescue cases show what funding and dilution could do, rather than assume away the problem.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
paragraphs: The issuer is Prime Cable Industries Limited, NSE PRIMECAB, ISIN INE0CQA01020, CIN L31905DL2008PLC177989. It was incorporated in 2008 as R C Cable Private Limited, acquired a promoter proprietorship in 2009, adopted its present name in 2019, became public in December 2024, and listed on NSE Emerge on 29 September 2025. It is not another similarly named cable company.

This assessment uses information through 20 October 2026, an official 19 October close of ₹192.35, and a five-year holding interval from 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031. Annualized returns use actual days divided by 365.25. The nominal pretax equity hurdle is 15%, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. The ₹5 lakh position is an illustrative liquidity test, not a suitable position for any particular investor.

Financial statements are standalone Indian accounting standards, not Ind AS; no subsidiary, joint venture or associate is reported for FY26. FY23–FY25 history uses the IPO restatement, FY21–FY22 uses earlier audited accounts, and FY26 uses its audited annual report. The statutory FY25 comparative in FY26 is not silently substituted for restated FY25.

G1 is Conditional because reported compliance improvements and promoter alignment coexist with disclosure inconsistencies. G2 is Hold because repeated bank-return and cost-record observations lack quantified resolution. G3 is Hold because an updated, committed funding bridge is not established. G4 is Conditional: actual trading is verified, but ESM Stage I, trade-for-trade settlement and the 1,600-share lot materially constrain implementation.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
paragraphs: Thirteen factors are audited below using the same definitions and original weights as framework v 3.0. Unknown does not mean average. REV, R and P are not scored; their weights are not redistributed. BQS, GQS and IAS are therefore NS, and their bounds are mathematical missing-data bounds rather than confidence intervals or point rankings.

Persistent poor cash realization triggers the GQS ceiling of 5.0. The raw GQS missing-data range is retained, its diagnostic upper bound is capped, and the final point score remains NS. A high sales CAGR cannot override this cash-quality ceiling.

CAP is not left unscored simply because private project cohorts are unavailable. A three-year operating-capital bridge links incremental standard-tax NOPAT to PPE, construction in progress and operating working capital. It supports a mixed score rather than an exceptional one. IAS uses the unrounded BQS when available; here missing-factor bounds and an optional propagated BQS range are shown separately.

Liquidity starts from the lower 60-session mean or median traded value. Its fractional result starts in the 9 band, but whole lots, restricted settlement, unverified spreads and concentration warrant an explicit downgrade to 3. None of these adjustments is treated as proof of governance misconduct.

sections.title: Business Overview
paragraphs: Prime manufactures low-voltage power and control cables, aerial-bunch cables, instrumentation products, wires and conductors for utilities, EPC contractors and private industrial customers. Manufacturing includes conductor processing, insulation, stranding, armouring and testing. BIS approvals, utility vendor qualification and laboratory capability matter more than consumer brand advertising in this institutional business.

FY26 product revenue was approximately ₹91.3 crore in control cables, ₹67.4 crore in power cables, ₹62.6 crore in aerial-bunch cables and ₹13.6 crore in other products. Aerial-bunch revenue rose especially quickly. Government and government-linked EPC business remained about 50.9% of revenue, versus 74.55% in FY25; private-sector diversification is meaningful but does not remove project and counterparty risk.

Customers buy tested cable specifications and dependable execution; raw-metal content is a substantial part of the invoice. Management says commodity escalation is reimbursed without additional margin. This reduces some raw-material price risk, but can inflate reported revenue, compress percentage margins and increase the cash needed to finance inventory and debtors.

The existing Narela and Ghiloth operations are being supplemented by a new medium-voltage facility. Expanding into up to 33 kV products can broaden tender eligibility and mix,  but the project adds commissioning, quality, approval and working-capital demands before its economics are proven.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
paragraphs: Vendor approvals in 20 states, longstanding institutional relationships, testing capability and qualification history create useful entry friction. These are genuine operating assets: a new supplier cannot instantly qualify for every utility tender. The company has also delivered a meaningful increase in production and broadened its product range.

The evidence does not establish durable pricing power. Tenders and competitive EPC procurement remain price-sensitive, suppliers lack comprehensive long-term contracts, and metal pass-through does not confer excess margin. Customer concentration is still high: the top 10 represented 55% of FY26 sales, despite improvement from 66.51%. These facts fit a contestable niche, not a structural franchise.

Three relevant listed operating comparators are V-Marc India, Dynamic Cables and Ultracab. The prospectus supplies their FY25 accounting ratios and September 2025 price multiples. Those stale multiples are context only, not a current peer valuation anchor. Dynamic and V-Marc have different scale and product mix; Ultracab provides a smaller-company comparison. No blanket premium to their multiples is assumed.

The terminal EV/EBITDA range of 7 x, 10 x and 13 x is an explicit analyst scenario for a capital-intensive, competitively tendered business. It is not imported from large branded leaders or represented as an observed October 2026 sector median. Qualification value could improve with repeat MV orders, but that requires evidence of margin and cash retention.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
paragraphs: The selected five-year nominal sales window is FY21–FY26; the three-year cross-check is FY23–FY26. Both are calculated from the preserved statements rather than selecting the most flattering start date. FY21 was a pandemic-disrupted base, and FY23–FY25 restatements do not create an economically comparable physical-volume series by themselves.

Sold volume rose from 7,193 km in FY23 to 8,491 km in FY24 and 14,447 km in FY25. This is important counterevidence to the claim that all sales growth is metal inflation. Revenue per sold kilometre also changes, however, because conductor metal, gauge, voltage and product mix are not standardized. The physical series spans only two annual growth intervals. The reported value-added residual also rises strongly, but its material/direct-cost and inventory components are precisely where repeated cost-record and book-to-bank concerns remain unresolved.

FY26 management reported 37,000 km capacity and 55% annual utilization; multiplying those numbers produces an approximate production quantity, not sold volume. The MD&A still refers to 34,000 km capacity. The prospectus capacity certification uses standard representative products and is not a homogeneous throughput measure. Those limitations prevent using the inferred output as a verified FY26 sales quantity.

Q1 FY27 provisional revenue of ₹93.2 crore versus ₹34.6 crore and a June order book of ₹210 crore support demand momentum. They do not establish audited trailing earnings, a four-quarter volume trend or a full-year cash result. The model uses that quarter explicitly and allocates only the residual scenario revenue to the rest of FY27; it never annualizes the quarter mechanically.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
paragraphs: The demand opportunity is credible: distribution modernization, utility expenditure, infrastructure, renewables and industrial electrification all use the product range. Medium-voltage capability expands the addressable tender pool. The accessible runway is narrower than a national TAM because customer approvals, production qualification, financing and execution constrain what Prime can win profitably.

The ₹39.9 crore project includes about ₹10.5 crore of land, ₹11.0 crore of construction and ₹18.4 crore of plant and machinery. Management envisaged 5,000 km additional capacity by H1 FY27 and more than 8,000 km by Q1 FY28, with utilization of 28% and 45% initially and 85% at peak. The funding plan references ₹14.5 crore IPO proceeds and ₹25.4 crore internal accruals and debt; this is a plan, not evidence of a committed new facility.

The operating-capital bridge uses PPE including CWIP plus inventory, receivables and other operating current assets, less trade and operating liabilities, excluding capital creditors. It compares standard 25%-tax NOPAT over FY23–FY26 against a 12%–16% cost-of-capital range. Current ROCE alone is not used as proof of attractive reinvestment. The latest one-year incremental result is weaker as money enters working capital and an unramped project.

Growth capex remaining is modeled as the announced total less identified land and deployed IPO-funded capex,  pending a project-by-project reconciliation. Capital creditors already recognized are paid separately once. Later growth beyond existing/new planned capacity also incurs additional capex. Bear cases do not magically cancel committed construction or release restricted cash for dividends.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
paragraphs: The promoter group held 12,546,964 shares, or 68.47%, at 30 September 2026. The current primary shareholding filing reports no promoter pledge, warrants, convertible securities or outstanding ESOPs. A similarly named PDF on the issuer website actually contains September 2025 data; its filename was not used to authenticate the latest ownership position.

Related-party financing is material: March 2026 promoter, director and relative loans were ₹9.4513 crore. The FY26 accounts disclose director remuneration of ₹1.218 crore, promoter-family interest of roughly ₹0.666 crore and related rent of ₹0.0484 crore. These are disclosed transactions, not evidence of diversion. Their terms and maturity flexibility nonetheless matter to minority holders and funding resilience.

The statutory auditor changed from R K Karwa & Associates to Mittal Goel & Associates in September 2024. The prospectus explains completion of the prior auditor’s two terms; a change alone is not an adverse finding. The FY24 original report contains an audit-trail modification. The prospectus says activation occurred on 17 June 2024, whereas the FY25 report says operation throughout the year. That timing needs reconciliation rather than an accusation.

Execution positives include the operating Ghiloth expansion, higher production, customer diversification and MV approvals. The next project’s commissioning target was H1 FY27, but a final commissioning and cost-to-complete disclosure was not established by the cutoff search. Order wins and certifications are not substitutes for commercial utilization, cash collection or on-budget delivery.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
paragraphs: FY26 revenue was ₹234.8768 crore, reported PBT ₹16.4954 crore and PAT ₹12.2386 crore. Other income was ₹0.9334 crore. A ₹2.00 crore extraordinary expense appears below pre-extraordinary PBT, but its nature was not sufficiently explained in the reviewed accounts, results and call. It is retained in reported earnings; the higher pre-charge EBITDA is a clearly labeled alternative, not a free normalization.

Operating cash flow was negative ₹13.2058 crore and reported purchase capex ₹19.2596 crore. The ₹4.2678 crore rise in capital creditors appears within operating-liability movements while the purchase line matches asset additions. An analytical reclassification reduces operating cash to negative ₹17.4736 crore and cash capex to ₹14.9918 crore, leaving FCF unchanged at negative ₹32.4654 crore. This is a classification analysis, not a claim that total cash is misstated.

Cash interest is classified in financing, not already included in reported CFO. FY26 analytical operating cash after the capital-creditor reclassification and ₹4.2592 crore of financing-classified cash interest is negative ₹21.7328 crore; after-interest FCF is negative ₹36.7246 crore. Across FY23–FY26, the corresponding adjusted operating cash is negative ₹26.1540 crore versus ₹21.6563 crore PAT, and after-interest FCF is negative ₹57.5271 crore.

Trade receivables were ₹70.5232 crore, including ₹0.4612 crore classified as significant credit risk beyond three years. FY25’s largest debtor represented 22.73% of receivables and the top 10 represented 86.89%. Management later reported collecting 85% of March receivables by June; that is constructive but unaudited and does not show new receivables or net borrowing. Confirmations and GST input reconciliation remain open in the notes.

The main FY26 opinion and IFC opinion are unmodified, with audit-trail operation reported throughout. The CARO annexure nevertheless says bank working-capital returns use estimates/general valuation that may differ from books, cost records are not systematically maintained, and third-party inventory is excluded from physical verification. FY25 repeats the first two issues, while its Board report says cost records were not applicable. No quantified bank reconciliation or specific subsequent cure was found. These are the reasons for G2 Hold, not the formatting artifact discussed below.

The EPS note uses the closing 183.24 lakh shares as its stated weighted average despite a midyear issue. This report shows closing-share PAT explicitly and leaves the statutory weighting question open. The P&L and inventory note were visually checked because the double-page layout can reorder extracted cells.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
paragraphs: The market bridge uses the official dated close and verified 18,324,060 shares. It presents October price against March financial data explicitly, rather than call the resulting EV contemporaneous. Restricted deposits, IPO capex money and offer escrow are not free equity cash. A signed cash surplus after the operating reserve is used; a shortfall is not floored away.

The valuation is a cash-linked earnings-EV model, not a price-target spreadsheet disconnected from financing. Every monthly interval contains revenue, EBITDA, depreciation, tax,  interest, working capital, growth and maintenance capex,  old creditors and taxes, principal, reserve, equity issuance and share count. It starts on 31 March 2026, so a pre-entry breach cannot be concealed by beginning only in October.

Documented March residual bank headroom is drawn once. IPO money can pay eligible project expenditure, not unrelated obligations. Existing capital creditors and the prospectus land schedule overlap; the base pays the recognized creditor amount and a separate stress adds the ₹1.0563 crore excess of the disclosed future land schedule. No double counting of both full balances as established independent debts occurs.

Every non-rescue case breaches the selected reserve and lacks a verified current funding bridge, so ordinary and non-rescue conditional IRRs and ordinary entry prices are null. Separate hypothetical rescues issue whole shares at 75% of each tested reference price, deduct 3% fees and fund interval uses before receipts. The pre-entry issuances are counterfactual recapitalization assumptions, not actual historical transactions. Returns after rescue are conditional illustrations only.

Entry-price solvers re-fund every candidate at 12%,15% and 18% hurdles, check finite bracket crossings and retain residuals. Reverse revenue and 5 x/10 x tests also buy incremental capacity at 7 x sales per unit of capital before the relevant fiscal-year interval. This turns a valuation requirement into a funded arithmetic condition, not proof that the additional customers, approvals, production or equity investors exist.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
paragraphs: A plausible impairment path is not merely a lower terminal multiple. Delayed receivables and metal-funded inventory consume bank capacity; the new facility absorbs cash before sufficient sales; interest and taxes still fall due; creditors and promoters seek repayment; equity must be issued below prevailing market value. Existing shareholders can suffer permanent dilution even if the company ultimately survives and grows.

The downside test cuts receivable, inventory and PPE recoveries while paying all recorded liabilities once and allowing partial contingent claims. It uses no extra valuation for operating land already in PPE and no separate real-estate premium on top of earnings EV. Book equity is not a liquidation floor, particularly when receivables are concentrated and specialized plant may sell below cost.

The ₹12.5405 crore contingent exposure combines bank guarantees and the ₹0.3112 crore UHBVNL dispute. A guarantee is not automatically a cash loss; the model does not book all guarantees as present debt. The legal outcome and invocation likelihood remain uncertain. Promoter debt repayment and uncommitted bank enhancement are tested explicitly rather than assumed harmless.

Trade-for-trade settlement, ESM Stage I and a large minimum lot can amplify a valuation loss through execution friction. A price near a circuit limit is not a promise that an investor can transact. Risk is therefore a combination of business cash needs, financing terms, valuation and tradability, not a single leverage ratio.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
paragraphs: A5 x or 10 x shareholder outcome over the exact five-year interval requires roughly 38% or 58% annual appreciation before investor taxes and costs. Sales or company market-cap growth of the same multiple is insufficient if new shares are issued. The tests therefore use terminal value divided by the fully diluted end share count, not the original count.

At the current price the hurdle depends on cash retention, profitable capacity expansion and the price of future capital. The favorable scenario assumes better collection, a successful MV mix shift, sustained margins and continuing paid-for capacity. None is established by a single order announcement or a national electrification story.

Reverse solver outputs and failures are preserved below. A missing crossing within the declared search bracket is reported as such, not disguised as a required solution at the endpoint. Even a numerical crossing is only a necessary modeled condition: qualification, construction time, product demand and investor availability can prevent execution.

Prime is not designated a compounder. That would require financially reliable, cash-realized growth, attractive incremental returns and financeable expansion over time. The present cash-quality ceiling and research gates prevent an exciting scale story from substituting for those conditions.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
paragraphs: First obtain a quantified bank-return-to-ledger reconciliation for FY25 and FY26, including stock, receivables, valuation basis and drawing power. Require an auditor-supported response on systematic cost records and reconcile FY24/FY25 audit-trail timing. Clear G2 only when the material differences and any financial consequences are bounded, not merely when management repeats that the main opinion is clean.

For funding, obtain the latest audited or reviewed balance sheet, facility sanction and utilization, restricted-cash schedule, IPO deployment, capital-creditor maturity and project cost-to-complete. Re-run the source-date cash bridge with actual subsequent receipts and payments. A signed plan funded through internal accruals and debt is not the same as a drawable commitment.

Track comparable sold tonnage or standardized cable volume, metal realization and product mix separately; receivable ageing and customer concentration; gross collections alongside newly generated receivables; and CFO after excluding capital-creditor effects. Two cash-generative half-years with stable ageing would be stronger evidence than sales growth alone.

Confirm MV commercial commissioning, commissioning cost and sustained utilization against the H1 FY27/Q1 FY28 milestones. Re-check ESM stage, active series, lot size, market maker and 20/60-session liquidity before any implementation analysis. The illustrative position and participation limit must be reset to the actual decision context.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
paragraphs: Final classification: Research Hold, with mixed business economics and material unclosed reliability and financing questions. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS. Quality, attractiveness and compounder rankings are excluded. A mathematical range is not an investable point score.

The immediate action is to wait for the specific reconciliations and updated funding evidence, not to buy because a hypothetical rescue case clears a return hurdle. Lower prices alone do not cure unreliable inputs or lack of committed financing. Conversely, satisfactory evidence and sustained cash collection could change the assessment without requiring the business narrative to collapse.

G1 and G4 remain Conditional rather than Fail: disclosed alignment, no reported fraud/default, verified actual trading and a functioning listed security are real counterevidence. ESM is a preventive market-surveillance mechanism, not an exchange finding of wrongdoing. The Hold should be removed or tightened on new evidence, not treated as permanent guilt.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
paragraphs: Primary material includes the FY21–FY26 accounts, FY20 comparative context, September 2025 prospectus and restatement, FY26 audited exchange results, May 2026 investor presentation and call, July 2026 operational update, September 2026 shareholding and capital reconciliation, and official NSE market and surveillance files. Source identifiers, dates, URLs, file hashes and page locators are preserved in the registers.

Key open items are the quantified bank reconciliation; treatment of systematic cost records; the extraordinary expense; correct weighted-average EPS; a comparable FY26 physical-sales bridge; current funding and restricted cash; project cost-to-complete and commissioning; capital-creditor/land overlap; and current order-book collections. Missing items remain missing rather than filled with neutral values.

Analyst assumptions include the 1 crore operating reserve, monthly prefunding convention,9% debt cost,25% tax,  recurring listed-company costs, future cash-cycle targets, growth/maintenance capex,  terminal multiples and hypothetical rescue pricing/fees. Reserve 0/2 crore, funding availability, working capital, capex,  interest, promoter repayment, terminal multiples and margins are tested. The reserve is an analyst prudence standard, not a covenant or observed default trigger.

Financial and market extracts are sufficient to reproduce the arithmetic without redistributing original source documents or personal shareholder identifiers. Reproduction checks calculate from preserved inputs; they do not independently certify the truth of issuer disclosures. All conclusions are limited to the stated cutoff.

name: Prime Cable Industries Limited
summary:
Prime Cable has demonstrated a real manufacturing scale-up, but revenue growth is not yet a reliable measure of underlying demand growth. Copper and aluminium reimbursement, a shift toward aerial-bunch cables, and a low pandemic base amplify nominal sales. The stronger claim is that sold cable length doubled between FY23 and FY25; the missing comparable physical-sales bridge and unresolved cost-record reliability prevent a clean underlying-growth score. An economic value-added cross-check is also supplied; the framework does not require tonnage mechanically.

The decisive obstacle is financing and cash realization. FY26 reported operating cash flow was negative ₹13.21 crore despite ₹12.24 crore profit. Receivables reached ₹70.52 crore, while most of the reported ₹12.87 crore cash was restricted or earmarked. A ₹39.9 crore expansion and rapid working-capital growth cannot be treated as self-financing merely because management expects strong sales.

Research Hold. Financial reliability and prospective funding gates remain on Hold, with no ordinary return or entry-price recommendation and no numerical ranking eligibility. This is not a finding of fraud, an observed default, or a prediction of insolvency. The explicit rescue cases show what funding and dilution could do, rather than assume away the problem.

evidence.finding: No new shares in latest capital audit; promoter group 12,546,964 shares/68.47%; no pledge, warrants, convertibles or ESOPs disclosed.

evidence.finding: Six-year financial inputs with original/restated basis separation, cash and operating-capital bridges.

evidence.finding: Restated PAT differs from statutory history; FY24 audit-trail modification and conflicting June 17 activation/full-FY25 timing.

evidence.locator: Prospectus printed 195–196; May 22 call discussion of raw-metal escalation and utilization
evidence.finding: Sold km 7193/8491/14447 in FY23/24/25;100% raw-price escalation reimbursement without extra margin; no comparable FY26 sold volume.

evidence.locator: Notes 4,7,9,15 and cash-flow statement; IPO utilization disclosure
evidence.finding: Total cash 12.8736; margin 3.0150; IPO capex earmark 9.7144; escrow.0391; accessible.1051. CC 38.8239 of 40; debt 51.5494; capital creditors 4.5617.

evidence.locator: Auditor report and CARO printed 85–92; notes 29–30; Board report
evidence.finding: Unmodified main/IFC opinions coexist with unquantified estimated bank returns, unsystematic cost records and third-party stock verification exclusion. Debtor/creditor confirmations and GST reconciliation open.
Board says cost records not applicable; CARO says required but not systematically maintained. Estimated bank returns may differ from books. Main and IFC unmodified, no reported default or fraud.

evidence.locator: Product mix,  customer mix and capacity disclosures; management discussion
evidence.finding: FY26 control 91.3,power 67.4,ABC 62.6,other 13.6; top 10 sales 55%; government/EPC 50.9%;37,000 capacity/55% utilization versus stale 34,000 MD&A.

evidence.locator: Project/capex sections, prospectus IPO deployment reconciliation
evidence.finding: 39.9 project;14.5 IPO plus 25.4 accrual/debt plan. MV commissioning target H1 FY27, further phase Q1 FY28. New committed loan sanction not established.

evidence.locator: Business, competition, approvals and management operating discussion
evidence.finding: Institutional qualification and 20-state approvals help entry, but competitive tendering, supplier concentration and no broad long-term supplier contracts limit pricing power.
Provisional Q1 revenue 93.2 versus 34.6; June orderbook 210; management 85% March-debtor recovery claim. No updated full cash-flow statement.

evidence.locator: Prospectus printed 107 land schedule; FY26 notes 4,9,23,31
evidence.finding: Future land instalments 2.809 in each FY27/FY28 overlap capital creditors; contingent BG 12.2293 plus UHBVNL claim.3112; promoter loans 9.4513.

evidence.locator: Historical operating-capital reconstruction and model assumptions
evidence.finding: Standard-tax incremental NOPAT/operating IC supports mixed CAP economics; no acquisition used to explain increase. New asset and metal-cycle effects limit inference.

evidence.locator: P&L printed 94, cash flow 95, Note 21 and Note 27; visual verification
evidence.finding: 2 crore extraordinary expense retained; inventory-change cells match notes after column visual check; EPS note closing denominator needs weighting reconciliation.
